newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end down 3.03 pct on politics, baht.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end down 3.03 pct on politics, baht.

text.p: Market disappointment over a limited cabinet reshuffle last week, tight liquidity and a further setback for the baht caused Thai stocks to fall for the third straight day on Monday, brokers said.
The composite SET index tumbled 18.91 points or 3.03 percent to 604.34 on thin 2.04 billion baht turnover. It was the indicator's lowest close since the baht's de facto devaluation on July 2.

"Investors lost confidence in the government, seeing the minor cabinet reshuffle last week of creating more squabbling among members in the coalition government," said Padermpob Songkroh of Nava Finance.

Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh on Friday brought in two outsiders to join his eight-month old government, which tried to weather growing public criticism of its handling of the Thai economic turmoil.
Brokers said apart from political worries, investors were also concerned about tight liquidity and sustained weakness of the baht.
